6.label: KEEP
6.text: Organisations that abandon everything from their history each time a new leader arrives lose the institutional knowledge, relationships and infrastructure that took years to build. Before building new, assess what was working, what has been buried and what needs restoring.

6.label: START and STOP together
6.text: Alignment needs the active removal of competing influences. Name what must go alongside what must be chosen: the choice is half of the alignment and the removal is the other half.

6.label: STOP · the strategic shelf
6.text: Audit the initiatives, products, partnerships and assumptions still drawing resources but no longer drawing belief, and name the two that need to be put away before the next move can land.

8.label: Testable objectives
8.text: Vague strategy goals cannot be evaluated, and a strategy that cannot be tested in real time cannot be corrected in real time. Build in a specific outcome, a defined timeframe and a clear way to know whether it is working.

9.label: Specific enough to be built
9.text: Great strategies are specific enough to be built. Vague vision produces vague results. Use the formula to make each Key Result precise enough to execute and check.

12.label: Stopping at convenient
12.text: Execution often stops at the convenient point: the easy quick wins get delivered and the structurally difficult changes are deferred, rationalised and eventually abandoned. A strategy that is 70% executed often produces almost none of the intended transformation, because the avoided 30% is where the leverage lives.

12.label: Claiming the destination early
12.text: Many organisations announce a new strategic direction before the systems, people and structures can support it, then spend the next phase defending a position they have not yet earned. Use this with the closing line on the slide.

13.label: What will feed or fight this
13.text: By the time a programme is announced, the culture that will carry it or starve it is already in place. Before launch, sit with the team that will execute it and ask: what in our current way of working will feed or fight this? Fix that before the launch date.

13.label: Know what you have
13.text: Organisations that enter a new strategy without a clear account of what they have, what capacity exists and where the real strengths lie are navigating without an accurate map. Take stock before planning what you will do.

14.label: Sequenced execution
14.text: Great strategies are sequenced: each phase prepares for the next. Trying to do everything at once is the fastest way to produce something that resembles nothing.

16.label: Differentiated strategy
16.text: Effective strategy addresses each team, unit and function with the specific truth about where they are and where they are headed. Generic strategy inspires no one because it is addressed to no one.

18.label: No governing centre
18.text: When each function, team and leader defines success by its own standard, the cumulative result is chaos. The absence of a shared governing framework produces the worst outcomes from the most sincere efforts. Use this with “Competing definitions of success across functions”.

20.label: Listening before acting
20.text: Leaders who listen collectively before acting ground their decisions in shared conviction. Use this with Step 4, the alignment test run publicly.

21.label: Protecting attention
21.text: Organisations often lose momentum because key people let peripheral demands consume the attention needed to finish. Strategic discipline includes deciding what will not receive executive time. Use this with the low-impact cells.

21.label: The capacity for distinction
21.text: Organisations that treat all risks as equivalent and all opportunities as equally weighted have lost an essential decision tool. Not everything deserves the same response.

22.label: Seniority and challenge
22.text: Seniority deserves respect and stays open to challenge. Healthy leaders create room for insight from different levels and generations.

27.label: The second cost
27.text: The leader who launches a strategic move without pricing every component retreats publicly when the second invoice arrives. Stress-test each initiative against the costs that do not appear on the deal sheet: the human responsibility, the cultural change and the long-term obligation. Use this when the group places items on the effort axis.

27.label: An open door is information
27.text: Not every available opportunity deserves automatic pursuit. Test each one against readiness, priorities, capacity and surrounding conditions.
